meta.title: IND-45 additive citizen evidence — Bengaluru khata default path
meta.disclaimer: Additive public first-person evidence only, not official advice or a municipal procedure. Personal details, usernames, precise locations, property identifiers, contact details, and payment amounts have been omitted.

scenarios.label: Draft or pending e-Khata
scenarios.summary: A property record is visible as a draft or has not reached a known final e-Khata state.

sources.title: E-khaata application glitch with BBMP E-Aasthi portal - whom to contact??
sources.notes: A citizen's first-person report of an e-Aasthi application. It describes a name-mismatch stage, an attempted supporting-document upload, repeat error messages after re-login, and no reported resolution through the initially contacted channels. It does not establish a current portal defect, a document requirement for other cases, an agency response obligation, or a general recovery route. Usernames, local-office detail, contact data, and payment detail are omitted.

sources.title: Ekhata issue - need help
sources.notes: A citizen's first-person account of a draft record in a prior holder's name, a rejected mutation component, and a final e-Khata subsequently issued in that prior holder's name. The author reports that the online correction path displayed a prior-holder eKYC condition and that they could not reapply after issuance. This is one account, not evidence of an eKYC rule, mutation sequence, fee rule, final-record effect, or universal correction barrier. Personal and property details are omitted.

claims.text: One citizen reported that an e-Aasthi application could not proceed past a name-mismatch stage because an attempted supporting-document upload repeatedly returned a re-login error and the next step then indicated that a deed document had not been uploaded.
claims.notes: A single self-report of a displayed state and failed action. The account does not distinguish a transient technical condition from user input, document format, authentication, or case-specific validation, and it reports no authoritative resolution.

claims.text: One citizen reported that after a final e-Khata issued in a prior holder's name, the online correction path displayed a condition that the prior holder's eKYC was not complete, leaving the citizen unable to complete that correction online.
claims.notes: The reported screen condition is case evidence only. It does not establish that prior-holder eKYC is generally required, that the record was legally incorrect, that final issuance always blocks reapplication, or that an offline or authorised recovery route is unavailable.

roadblocks.title: Reported supporting-document upload and validation dead end
roadblocks.symptom: A citizen reports that an attempted upload produced a repeat re-login error while the next step still required a deed document.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; the account cannot distinguish portal availability, session state, document selection, file handling, authentication, or case-specific validation.
roadblocks.recovery: No authoritative recovery outcome was reported. Preserve the displayed messages and seek authorised, case-specific support; do not infer a general document checklist or workaround from this account.

roadblocks.title: Reported online correction block after prior-holder final record
roadblocks.symptom: A citizen reports receiving a final e-Khata in a prior holder's name and seeing a prior-holder eKYC condition on the online correction path.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; the account does not establish record ownership, the correction policy, the eKYC condition's applicability, or whether another authorised route can resolve the case.
roadblocks.recovery: No completed recovery was reported. Obtain authorised, property-specific guidance on the issued record and correction state; do not generalise the reported eKYC condition or rely on informal workarounds.
